quests.question: My colleague and I finished the report two days early.
quests.sentence: My colleague and I finished the report two days early.
quests.hint: Find the doer right before finished, noticing the subject pronoun I, not me.
quests.explanation: My colleague and I is the doer of finished, using the subject pronoun I since it performs the action. In passive voice, this same idea shifts I into the object pronoun me: The report was finished two days early by my colleague and me.
quests.activeVoice: My colleague and I finished the report two days early.
quests.passiveVoice: The report was finished two days early by my colleague and me.

quests.question: The award was presented to us at last year's ceremony.
quests.sentence: The award was presented to us at last year's ceremony.
quests.hint: Notice the object pronoun us here, not we. Ask who received the award, not who gave it.
quests.explanation: Us (receiver, as the object of to) is used because it follows the preposition to in this passive structure - the presenters remain unnamed. Switching to active voice requires flipping us back into the subject pronoun we: They presented the award to us at last year's ceremony.
quests.activeVoice: They presented the award to us at last year's ceremony.
quests.passiveVoice: The award was presented to us at last year's ceremony.

quests.question: We were given very little warning before the office closed for renovations.
quests.sentence: We were given very little warning before the office closed for renovations.
quests.hint: We here is the subject, but check whether we performed the giving or received it.
quests.explanation: We (receiver) were given - even though we is a subject pronoun, it doesn't mean the sentence is active; the subject can still be the receiver of an action in passive voice. No one is named as responsible. Active form: They gave us very little warning before the office closed for renovations.
quests.activeVoice: They gave us very little warning before the office closed for renovations.
quests.passiveVoice: We were given very little warning before the office closed for renovations.

quests.question: The board eventually promoted him to senior partner after years of strong performance.
quests.sentence: The board eventually promoted him to senior partner after years of strong performance.
quests.hint: Find the doer right before promoted, noticing the object pronoun him, not he.
quests.explanation: The board is the doer of promoted, with him as the object pronoun since he receives the action here. Flipping to passive moves him into subject position, where it becomes he: He was eventually promoted to senior partner after years of strong performance.
quests.activeVoice: The board eventually promoted him to senior partner after years of strong performance.
quests.passiveVoice: He was eventually promoted to senior partner after years of strong performance by the board.

quests.question: She was warned twice about the missing paperwork before the deadline passed.
quests.sentence: She was warned twice about the missing paperwork before the deadline passed.
quests.hint: Notice the subject pronoun she here. Ask whether she performed the warning or received it.
quests.explanation: She (receiver) was warned - even as the subject, she receives the action rather than performing it, which is exactly what makes this passive. No one is named as the one who warned her. Active form: They warned her twice about the missing paperwork before the deadline passed.
quests.activeVoice: They warned her twice about the missing paperwork before the deadline passed.
quests.passiveVoice: She was warned twice about the missing paperwork before the deadline passed.

quests.question: The interviewer asked her several unexpected questions about her previous job.
quests.sentence: The interviewer asked her several unexpected questions about her previous job.
quests.hint: Find the doer right before asked, noticing the object pronoun her.
quests.explanation: The interviewer is the doer of asked, with her as the object pronoun. Passive version moves her into subject position as she: She was asked several unexpected questions about her previous job by the interviewer.
quests.activeVoice: The interviewer asked her several unexpected questions about her previous job.
quests.passiveVoice: She was asked several unexpected questions about her previous job by the interviewer.

quests.question: The landlord evicted them without following the proper legal process.
quests.sentence: The landlord evicted them without following the proper legal process.
quests.hint: Find the doer right before evicted, noticing the object pronoun them.
quests.explanation: The landlord is the doer of evicted, with them as the object pronoun. Passive version moves them into subject position as they: They were evicted without the proper legal process being followed.
quests.activeVoice: The landlord evicted them without following the proper legal process.
quests.passiveVoice: They were evicted without the proper legal process being followed by the landlord.

quests.question: They were misinformed about the actual cost of the repairs.
quests.sentence: They were misinformed about the actual cost of the repairs.
quests.hint: They here is the subject, but check whether they performed the informing or received it.
quests.explanation: They (receiver) were misinformed - even as the subject pronoun, they receives the action rather than performing it. No one is named as responsible. Active form: Someone misinformed them about the actual cost of the repairs.
quests.activeVoice: Someone misinformed them about the actual cost of the repairs.
quests.passiveVoice: They were misinformed about the actual cost of the repairs.

quests.question: The single error affects every calculation that follows it in the spreadsheet.
quests.sentence: The single error affects every calculation that follows it in the spreadsheet.
quests.hint: Check subject-verb agreement here: the single error, singular, takes affects, not affect. Find the doer right before it.
quests.explanation: The single error is the doer of affects, correctly matched in number since a singular subject takes a singular present-tense verb. Passive version: Every calculation that follows it in the spreadsheet is affected by the single error.
quests.activeVoice: The single error affects every calculation that follows it in the spreadsheet.
quests.passiveVoice: Every calculation that follows it in the spreadsheet is affected by the single error.

quests.question: One mistake in the code caused several other functions to fail.
quests.sentence: One mistake in the code caused several other functions to fail.
quests.hint: Notice that one mistake is singular, but several other functions is plural. Find the doer right before caused.
quests.explanation: One mistake is the singular doer of caused, even though its effect touches several other functions, a plural object - the verb agrees with the subject, not the object. Passive version, keeping the same relationship: Several other functions were caused to fail by one mistake in the code.
quests.grammarRule: Active with Singular Subject, Plural Object
quests.activeVoice: One mistake in the code caused several other functions to fail.
quests.passiveVoice: Several other functions were caused to fail by one mistake in the code.

quests.question: Several minor errors were traced back to a single faulty sensor.
quests.sentence: Several minor errors were traced back to a single faulty sensor.
quests.hint: Notice that several minor errors is plural, but a single faulty sensor is singular. Look for were plus a past participle, agreeing with the plural subject.
quests.explanation: Several minor errors (receiver, plural) were traced - the passive verb were agrees with the plural subject, even though the agent, a single faulty sensor, is singular. Active form: A single faulty sensor caused several minor errors, which were traced back to it (more directly: Someone traced several minor errors back to a single faulty sensor).
quests.grammarRule: Passive with Plural Subject, Singular Agent
quests.activeVoice: Someone traced several minor errors back to a single faulty sensor.
quests.passiveVoice: Several minor errors were traced back to a single faulty sensor.

quests.question: The manager, not the two assistants, approved the final budget.
quests.sentence: The manager, not the two assistants, approved the final budget.
quests.hint: Check agreement carefully: the manager is singular, so the verb approved must match that, not the two assistants. Find the doer right before approved.
quests.explanation: The manager is the singular doer of approved - the phrase not the two assistants is simply clarifying who did not do the approving, without changing subject-verb agreement. Passive version: The final budget was approved by the manager, not the two assistants.
quests.activeVoice: The manager, not the two assistants, approved the final budget.
quests.passiveVoice: The final budget was approved by the manager, not the two assistants.

quests.question: The coach criticized the referee after the controversial call.
quests.sentence: The coach criticized the referee after the controversial call.
quests.hint: Find the doer right before criticized - who is doing the criticizing, and who receives it?
quests.explanation: The coach is the doer of criticized, acting on the referee, the receiver. A common learner mistake would be reversing these roles in the passive version - the correct passive keeps the same relationship: The referee was criticized by the coach after the controversial call, not The coach was criticized by the referee.
quests.activeVoice: The coach criticized the referee after the controversial call.
quests.passiveVoice: The referee was criticized by the coach after the controversial call.

quests.question: The tenant was sued by the landlord over unpaid rent.
quests.sentence: The tenant was sued by the landlord over unpaid rent.
quests.hint: Find the receiver and the doer carefully - who took legal action, and who faced it?
quests.explanation: The tenant (receiver) was sued - the landlord is the one who took action, named correctly after by. A meaning-changing error would flip these roles: The landlord was sued by the tenant would describe a completely different situation. Active form: The landlord sued the tenant over unpaid rent.
quests.activeVoice: The landlord sued the tenant over unpaid rent.
quests.passiveVoice: The tenant was sued by the landlord over unpaid rent.

quests.question: The customer thanked the barista for remembering her usual order.
quests.sentence: The customer thanked the barista for remembering her usual order.
quests.hint: Find the doer right before thanked - who is expressing thanks, and who receives it?
quests.explanation: The customer is the doer of thanked, acting toward the barista, the receiver. Reversing these roles in passive voice would change the meaning entirely - the correct version keeps them in place: The barista was thanked by the customer for remembering her usual order.
quests.activeVoice: The customer thanked the barista for remembering her usual order.
quests.passiveVoice: The barista was thanked by the customer for remembering her usual order.

quests.question: After the accident, the driver blamed himself for not checking his mirrors.
quests.sentence: After the accident, the driver blamed himself for not checking his mirrors.
quests.hint: Notice himself refers back to the driver, the same person. Find the doer right before blamed.
quests.explanation: The driver is the doer of blamed, with himself as a reflexive object referring back to the same person - reflexive verbs like this rarely appear in natural passive voice, since it would sound odd to say He was blamed by himself. Active voice is simply the natural choice here.
quests.grammarRule: Active with Reflexive Object (No Natural Passive)
quests.activeVoice: After the accident, the driver blamed himself for not checking his mirrors.
quests.passiveVoice: No natural passive form exists here; reflexive constructions like this typically stay active.

quests.question: The witnesses were questioned separately so their stories couldn't influence each other.
quests.sentence: The witnesses were questioned separately so their stories couldn't influence each other.
quests.hint: The witnesses is the subject here - check whether they performed the questioning or received it.
quests.explanation: The witnesses (receiver) were questioned - the pronoun their later in the sentence correctly refers back to the witnesses, keeping the reference clear across both clauses. No specific detective is named. Active form: Detectives questioned the witnesses separately so their stories couldn't influence each other.
quests.activeVoice: Detectives questioned the witnesses separately so their stories couldn't influence each other.
quests.passiveVoice: The witnesses were questioned separately so their stories couldn't influence each other.

quests.question: The two rival companies eventually agreed to merge their operations.
quests.sentence: The two rival companies eventually agreed to merge their operations.
quests.hint: Notice their refers back to the two rival companies, correctly plural. Find the doer right before agreed.
quests.explanation: The two rival companies is the doer of agreed, with their correctly matching in number since it refers back to a plural subject. This kind of reciprocal agreement rarely takes a natural passive form, since agree to merge describes a mutual action rather than one performed on a clear receiver.
quests.grammarRule: Active with Plural Pronoun Reference (No Natural Passive)
quests.activeVoice: The two rival companies eventually agreed to merge their operations.
quests.passiveVoice: No natural passive form exists here; mutual or reciprocal actions like this typically stay active.

quests.question: The teacher returned their essays with detailed comments in the margins.
quests.sentence: The teacher returned their essays with detailed comments in the margins.
quests.hint: Notice their refers to the students, implied by context, not to the teacher. Find the doer right before returned.
quests.explanation: The teacher is the doer of returned, with their essays as the object - their refers to the students who own the essays, not to the teacher. Passive version, keeping that same reference clear: Their essays were returned with detailed comments in the margins by the teacher.
quests.activeVoice: The teacher returned their essays with detailed comments in the margins.
quests.passiveVoice: Their essays were returned with detailed comments in the margins by the teacher.

quests.question: His proposal was rejected by the committee after a lengthy debate.
quests.sentence: His proposal was rejected by the committee after a lengthy debate.
quests.hint: His here refers to a specific person mentioned earlier or understood from context. Look for was plus a past participle.
quests.explanation: His proposal (receiver) was rejected - his correctly shows ownership of the proposal, distinct from the committee, which performs the rejecting. Active form: The committee rejected his proposal after a lengthy debate.
quests.activeVoice: The committee rejected his proposal after a lengthy debate.
quests.passiveVoice: His proposal was rejected by the committee after a lengthy debate.

quests.question: Her manager praised her initiative during the team meeting.
quests.sentence: Her manager praised her initiative during the team meeting.
quests.hint: Notice both her (possessive) and her (object) appear here, but only one is the true grammatical object. Find the doer right before praised.
quests.explanation: Her manager is the doer of praised, with her initiative as the object - the first her shows possession (whose initiative), while initiative itself is what receives the praise. Passive version: Her initiative was praised by her manager during the team meeting.
quests.grammarRule: Active with Possessive and Object Pronoun
quests.activeVoice: Her manager praised her initiative during the team meeting.
quests.passiveVoice: Her initiative was praised by her manager during the team meeting.

quests.question: The prize was shared equally between him and her after the tie.
quests.sentence: The prize was shared equally between him and her after the tie.
quests.hint: Notice both pronouns here are object pronouns, him and her, correctly following the preposition between. Look for was plus a past participle.
quests.explanation: The prize (receiver) was shared - between takes object pronouns, so him and her are correct here; a common learner error would be writing he and she instead, which would be ungrammatical after a preposition. Active form: The judges shared the prize equally between him and her after the tie.
quests.grammarRule: Passive with Pronoun Case After Preposition
quests.activeVoice: The judges shared the prize equally between him and her after the tie.
quests.passiveVoice: The prize was shared equally between him and her after the tie.

quests.question: He and I were both interviewed for the same position last week.
quests.sentence: He and I were both interviewed for the same position last week.
quests.hint: Notice both pronouns here are subject pronouns, he and I, correctly used since they are the subject. Look for were plus a past participle.
quests.explanation: He and I (receiver, as subject pronouns) were interviewed - even though he and I sit in subject position, they still receive the action, which is what makes this passive despite using subject-case pronouns; a common error would be swapping in him and me here since the sentence feels like it should take object pronouns. Active form: Someone interviewed him and me for the same position last week.
quests.grammarRule: Passive with Subject Pronoun as Receiver
quests.activeVoice: Someone interviewed him and me for the same position last week.
quests.passiveVoice: He and I were both interviewed for the same position last week.

quests.question: The manager gave my colleague and me conflicting instructions on the same project.
quests.sentence: The manager gave my colleague and me conflicting instructions on the same project.
quests.hint: Notice my colleague and me uses the object pronoun me, correctly, since it follows the verb gave. Find the doer right before gave.
quests.explanation: The manager is the doer of gave, with my colleague and me as the two-part indirect object - me is correct here since it functions as an object, not a subject; a common error would be writing my colleague and I instead. Passive version: My colleague and I were given conflicting instructions on the same project by the manager.
quests.activeVoice: The manager gave my colleague and me conflicting instructions on the same project.
quests.passiveVoice: My colleague and I were given conflicting instructions on the same project by the manager.

quests.question: They should have been told about the schedule change days in advance.
quests.sentence: They should have been told about the schedule change days in advance.
quests.hint: They here is the subject, but check whether they performed the telling or received it.
quests.explanation: They (receiver) should have been told - even as a subject pronoun, they receives the action in this modal perfect passive, with no specific department named. Active form: Someone should have told them about the schedule change days in advance.
quests.activeVoice: Someone should have told them about the schedule change days in advance.
quests.passiveVoice: They should have been told about the schedule change days in advance.

quests.question: He and his brother have run this small hardware store for over twenty years.
quests.sentence: He and his brother have run this small hardware store for over twenty years.
quests.hint: Notice he and his brother is a compound subject, correctly plural for the verb have run. Find the doer right before have run.
quests.explanation: He and his brother is the doer of have run, a compound subject taking the plural verb form have, present perfect active. This kind of long-term personal ownership rarely takes a natural passive form, since it would feel unnatural to say This small hardware store has been run by him and his brother for over twenty years - though technically grammatical, active voice suits this context better.
quests.activeVoice: He and his brother have run this small hardware store for over twenty years.
quests.passiveVoice: This small hardware store has been run by him and his brother for over twenty years.

quests.question: Neither the manager nor the assistants were informed about the last-minute change.
quests.sentence: Neither the manager nor the assistants were informed about the last-minute change.
quests.hint: Check agreement here: neither...nor usually agrees with the noun closest to the verb, assistants, hence were. Look for were plus a past participle.
quests.explanation: Neither the manager nor the assistants (receiver) were informed - the verb agrees with assistants, the noun closest to it, following the neither...nor agreement rule, even though manager is singular. No one is named as responsible. Active form: Someone informed neither the manager nor the assistants about the last-minute change.
quests.activeVoice: Someone informed neither the manager nor the assistants about the last-minute change.
quests.passiveVoice: Neither the manager nor the assistants were informed about the last-minute change.

quests.question: This checkpoint reviews pronouns and agreement: The director thanked the entire crew and me personally after the final show.
quests.sentence: This checkpoint reviews pronouns and agreement: The director thanked the entire crew and me personally after the final show.
quests.hint: Find the doer right before thanked, noticing the object pronoun me.
quests.explanation: This checkpoint reviews active voice with a compound object: the director is the doer of thanked, with the entire crew and me as the object, correctly using me rather than I since it follows the verb. Passive version: The entire crew and I were thanked personally by the director after the final show.
quests.activeVoice: The director thanked the entire crew and me personally after the final show.
quests.passiveVoice: The entire crew and I were thanked personally by the director after the final show.

quests.question: This checkpoint reviews pronouns and agreement: She and her assistant were never officially notified of the delay.
quests.sentence: This checkpoint reviews pronouns and agreement: She and her assistant were never officially notified of the delay.
quests.hint: She and her assistant is the subject here - check whether they performed the notifying or received it.
quests.explanation: This checkpoint reviews passive voice with a compound subject: she and her assistant (receiver) were notified, correctly using subject pronouns even though they receive the action. No one is named as responsible. Active form: Nobody ever officially notified her and her assistant of the delay.
quests.activeVoice: Nobody ever officially notified her and her assistant of the delay.
quests.passiveVoice: She and her assistant were never officially notified of the delay.

quests.question: This checkpoint reviews pronouns and agreement: Neither the parents nor the teacher was aware of the field trip cancellation.
quests.sentence: This checkpoint reviews pronouns and agreement: Neither the parents nor the teacher was aware of the field trip cancellation.
quests.hint: Check agreement here: neither...nor usually agrees with the noun closest to the verb, teacher, hence was, not were. Confirm this is active by checking whether anything is being done to the subject.
quests.explanation: This checkpoint reviews subject-verb agreement in active voice: the verb was agrees with teacher, the noun closest to it, even though parents is plural - and since aware describes a state rather than an action done to the subject, this sentence has no passive equivalent at all.
quests.grammarRule: Active with Neither/Nor Agreement (No Passive Possible)
quests.activeVoice: Neither the parents nor the teacher was aware of the field trip cancellation.
quests.passiveVoice: No passive form exists - aware describes a state, not an action performed on an object.
